reference_audit.finding: Existing CUDA.jl copyto! may automatically enable peer access and uses an asynchronous driver path. Study retains framework allocation but calls the same shared CUDART cudaMemcpyDefault API as native, with explicit both-device completion fences. Original native timer lacks those fences.

algorithm: Sequential CUDA-runtime host ring copies0->1->0 with end-of-region completion onbothdevices

scientific_intent.governing_method: Sequential device ring copies viaCUDA runtime
scientific_intent.precision_sensitivity: Integer data copied exactly; no floating arithmetic

allocation_interoperability_repair.precise_driver_mechanism: Not independently profiled; controlled allocation-policy effect recorded

observation: This is a real two-device ring, separate from the single-V100 performance population. Both buffers are checked in full after every trial. All four versions call the same shared CUDART cudaMemcpyDefault function and fence both devices at the end of the measured region; no peer-enable calls are issued. Framework versions differ in allocation API, not translated kernels. Original timing without an explicit completion guarantee and the prior one-device self-copy diagnostic are not completed-transfer measurements.
effort_observation: First CUDA.jl/KA host programs fail with CUDART invalid-value when using default stream-ordered pooled allocations. A guarded four-element diagnostic succeeds with JULIA_CUDA_MEMORY_POOL=none; allocation policy changes outside timing. Device-kernel count remains0; this is a runtime interoperation repair, not a framework feature unsupported claim.
